items.stem: Define the term 'HTML'.
items.answer: HyperText Markup Language: the language of tags used to define the structure and content of a web page.

items.stem: Explain why an external style sheet is preferred for a large website.
items.answer: All pages link to one file, so the look of every page is consistent and can be changed by editing one file; pages download faster because the CSS is cached.
items.markingKey: 1 mark consistency; 1 mark single place to change; 1 mark caching/smaller pages. [3]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a class selector and an id selector.
items.answer: A class can be applied to many elements and is written .name; an id identifies one unique element and is written #name, and has higher specificity.

items.stem: Pioneer Insurance in Bogotá wants its 40-page website to have a consistent style. Describe the purpose of the <head> and <body> sections of an HTML page.
items.answer: Head: metadata, title, links to CSS/scripts. Body: visible content.

items.stem: TransGlobal Logistics in Hanoi wants its 40-page website to have a consistent style. Assess the use of a single external style sheet for the whole website of TransGlobal Logistics.
items.answer: Points for: consistency; easy updates; smaller pages; caching. items.stem: Explain why "5" + 2 gives "52" in JavaScript but "5" * 2 gives 10.

items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: An operator that gives the remainder after one number is divided by another. [2]

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'modulus operator (%)' and 'const'.
items.answer: modulus operator (%): An operator that gives the remainder after one number is divided by another. const: A keyword that declares a variable whose value cannot be reassigned after it is set.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: modulus operator (%) correctly described; 1 mark: const correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain two advantages of using functions in JavaScript. (b) Explain why "5" + 2 gives "52" in JavaScript but "5" * 2 gives 10.
items.answer: (a) Code can be reused by calling the function many times; programs are easier to read, test and maintain because tasks are split into named parts; parameters let the same code work with different values. (b) With + and a string operand JavaScript concatenates, turning 2 into "2"; * is only numeric, so "5" is converted to the number 5 and multiplied.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4] (b) 1 mark + concatenates with strings; 1 mark * converts to number. [2]

items.stem: SkyLink Airways in Auckland wants a JavaScript price calculator on its booking page. Explain the difference between a variable and a constant.
items.answer: Variable can change while the program runs; constant is fixed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [2]
inner call 3 × 3 + 3 = 12; outer call 12 × 3 + 3 = 39 — 39 [2]

items.stem: TransGlobal Logistics in Santiago wants a JavaScript price calculator on its booking page. (a) Write a JavaScript function total(price, qty) that returns the price multiplied by the quantity. (b) State three JavaScript data types with an example of each.
items.answer: (a) function total(price, qty) { return price * qty; } (b) Number (42), String ("Lima"), Boolean (true), Array ([1,2]), Object.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark header with parameters; 1 mark return of product. [2] (b) 1 mark each, max 3. [3]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Define the term 'Document Object Model (DOM)'. (b) Define the term 'innerHTML'.
items.answer: (a) A tree structure in which the browser represents every element of a web page, which JavaScript can read and change. (b) A property of an element that holds the HTML content inside it; setting it changes what is displayed.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A tree structure in which the browser represents every element of a web page, which JavaScript can read and change. [2] (b) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A property of an element that holds the HTML content inside it; setting it changes what is displayed. [2]

items.stem: Distinguish between 'getElementById' and 'event handler'.
items.answer: getElementById: A DOM method that returns the element with a given id so that its content or style can be changed. event handler: A function that runs when a particular event happens, such as a button being clicked (onclick) or a key being pressed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: getElementById correctly described; 1 mark: event handler correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets in Hanoi wants a web page that counts visitors' clicks and shows messages. Write a loop that outputs the numbers 1 to 10.
items.answer: for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { console.log(i); }
items.markingKey: 1 mark loop range; 1 mark output inside loop. [2]

items.stem: Lakeside College in Accra wants a web page that counts visitors' clicks and shows messages. (a) Explain what is meant by the DOM. (b) Write JavaScript that displays "Correct!" in an element with id "result". (c) Explain how an event handler is used for a button.
items.answer: (a) Tree representation of page elements that scripts can access and change. (b) document.getElementById("result").innerHTML = "Correct!"; (c) onclick attribute/addEventListener calls a function when clicked.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark tree of elements; 1 mark accessed/changed by JS. [2] (b) 1 mark getElementById; 1 mark innerHTML assignment. [2] (c) 1 mark event; 1 mark function runs. [2]

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'isNaN()' and 'client-side validation'.
items.answer: isNaN(): A JavaScript function that returns true if a value is not a number (cannot be converted to a number). client-side validation: Checking form input in the browser, using JavaScript or HTML attributes, before the data is sent to the server.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: isNaN() correctly described; 1 mark: client-side validation correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): Server-side validation is still needed. Reason (R): Client-side checks can be bypassed. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A is true and R explains why A is true.

items.stem: Hana is creating an online registration form for Palm Grove Hotel in Cape Town. Describe two checks JavaScript could carry out on the form.
items.answer: Presence (not empty); range (age 18–99); type (isNaN); format of email/phone with regular expressions; password length.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Lina is creating an online registration form for Starlight Cinemas in Karachi. Assess relying on JavaScript validation for the booking form of Starlight Cinemas.
items.answer: Points for: instant feedback; fewer errors; less server load. Points against / limitations: can be bypassed; inconsistent browser behaviour; security risk if server trusts data. Conclusion: use JavaScript for usability and always repeat validation on the server.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: instant feedback; fewer errors; less server load. Against: can be bypassed; inconsistent browser behaviour; security risk if server trusts data. Conclusion may argue: use JavaScript for usability and always repeat validation on the server. [4]
